summary: This standards-track document describes a YANG data model for the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol. It covers both version 2 and version 3 of VRRP. Operators can use it to configure and monitor VRRP in a standard way.

eli5.summary: If one helper goes home, a backup takes over so work never stops. This is a standard form for setting up and checking those backup helpers on routers.

subtitle: A standard YANG model for configuring, monitoring and getting alerts from VRRP, versions 2 and 3.

tldr.problem: VRRP lets routers share a virtual router and elect one to take over, but operators needed a standard, programmatic way to configure it and read its state.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the ietf-vrrp YANG module. It augments the interface and IP models with per-instance configuration, adds operational state and statistics, and defines three notifications.
tldr.outcome: One model covers both VRRP version 2 (IPv4) and version 3 (IPv4 and IPv6), usable over management protocols such as NETCONF. IANA registered the module and its XML namespace.

today: RFC 8347 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2018. It has not been obsoleted or updated, so it remains the definition of the ietf-vrrp YANG module.

sections.title: What the Model Is For
sections.content:
This document introduces a YANG data model (RFC 6020, RFC 7950) for the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP, RFC 3768 and RFC 5798). VRRP provides higher resiliency through an election protocol that dynamically assigns responsibility for a virtual router to one of the VRRP routers on a LAN.

The module supports both versions. VRRP version 2 supports IPv4, and version 3 supports both IPv4 and IPv6. With a suitable management protocol, the model can be used to configure VRRP, manage its operational behavior, retrieve its operational status and receive its notifications.
sections.eli5: Routers can back each other up like a substitute teacher. This document is a standard sheet for telling them how to do it and asking how it is going.

sections.title: How the Model Fits Existing Models
sections.content:
The module augments the interface model ietf-interfaces (RFC 8343) and the IP management model ietf-ip (RFC 8344). A vrrp container is added under the IPv4 or IPv6 part of an interface, and holds a list of vrrp-instance nodes keyed by vrid.

Each vrrp-instance represents a VRRP router state machine as described in Section 6.4 of RFC 5798. It holds configuration and state for the election process of a virtual router. The real addresses on the interface are the ones the VRRP router operates through, and the addresses of the virtual router are a list of IPv4 or IPv6 addresses under the instance.

The model conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA, RFC 8342). Operational state is combined with configuration in the same hierarchy, so a read from the operational datastore returns both rw and ro nodes.
sections.eli5: The VRRP form is stapled onto the existing network card form, so everything about one network connection stays together in one place.

sections.title: Configurable Settings
sections.content:
The model lets operators configure a VRRP instance (version 2 or 3), the virtual IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, tracked interfaces to detect interface failures and tracked networks to detect network failures.

Per instance, the main settings and defaults in the YANG module are listed below.

  • vrid: virtual router ID, range 1 to 255.
  • version: required, VRRP version 2 or 3.
  • priority: range 1 to 254, default 100.
  • preempt: enabled by default, with a hold-time of 0 seconds by default.
  • accept-mode: version 3 only, default false.
  • advertise-interval-sec for version 2: range 1 to 254 seconds, default 1.
  • advertise-interval-centi-sec for version 3: range 1 to 4095 centiseconds, default 100.

Tracked interfaces and networks carry a priority-decrement (range 1 to 254, default 10) that lowers the router's priority when the tracked item fails.
sections.eli5: You can set how important each backup helper is, how often they check in, and what to do if a road they watch gets blocked.

sections.title: Operational State and Statistics
sections.content:
Each instance reports read-only state: the current state (the module defines identities initialize, backup and master), whether it is-owner of the address, the source of the last advertisement, uptime, master-down-interval, skew-time, the last event and the reason for the latest transition to master.

The new-master reason is one of not-master, priority, preempted or no-response. Per-instance counters include master transitions, advertisements sent and received, priority-zero packets, invalid-type packets and packet-length errors. Two further counters, interval errors and address-list errors, are tied to optional features.

A global section summarizes the number of virtual routers and interfaces. It also counts checksum, version, VRID and IP TTL errors, with a discontinuity-datetime showing when counting restarted.
sections.eli5: You can ask each backup helper whether it is the boss right now, how many messages it has sent, and why it became boss last time.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.content:
The model defines three VRRP notifications.

  • vrrp-new-master-event: a new master has been elected. It carries the master's IP address and the reason.
  • vrrp-protocol-error-event: a message failed to reach a VRRP instance to be processed.
  • vrrp-virtual-router-error-event: an error for a message processed on a VRRP instance. It names the interface, the VRID and the error reason.

For other notifications, the mechanisms in the Subscribed-Notifications and YANG-Push drafts can be used. They allow per-client subscriptions, subtree or XPath filters, and periodic or on-demand delivery.
sections.eli5: The routers can ring a bell when a new boss takes over or when something goes wrong, so nobody has to keep asking.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The data is designed to be accessed over NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF. The mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH for NETCONF and TLS for RESTCONF, and the NETCONF access control model can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

The writable vrrp-instance subtrees under IPv4 and IPv6 are sensitive. Unauthorized writes can affect the routing subsystem of the local device and the network, causing malfunctions or delivery of packets to inappropriate destinations. Read access to /ietf-vrrp:vrrp and the same subtrees can disclose VRRP operational state.

IANA registered the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-vrrp and the YANG module ietf-vrrp with prefix vrrp.
sections.eli5: Only trusted people should be allowed to change the backup plan, because a wrong change could send traffic to the wrong place.
